meta.layer: Settlement and routes (D-026): dated settled places
meta.grain: post_office = one post-office record; urban_2500 = one Gibson urban place (place + state)

fields.year_established: post_office: first year of the record (Established); urban_2500: first census year with >= 2,500 people (a proxy, not a founding date)
fields.year_discontinued: post_office: Discontinued (null = open past the data); a rename also closes a record. urban_2500: null
fields.gnis_dist: GNIS name-match score of the post office (0.75-1; null = not given). Town-level point, office moves not recorded
fields.pop: urban_2500: population by census year (Gibson 1998); years not listed are absent
fields.carried_1840: urban_2500: urban in 1830, absent from the 1840 top-100 list (cut at 4,226), kept as urban in 1840 with no population
fields.po_id: urban_2500: post-office record that gave the coordinates (exact name + state match); null where coord_source = override
fields.coord_source: urban_2500: post_office = point of the exactly matched office; override = hand coordinates from research/urban_coords_override.csv (R9 section 5), which win over the match
fields.coord_ref: urban_2500: source of the point (GNIS feature id or landmark) for overrides; the office record for matches
fields.unverified: urban_2500: true where the hand point is a landmark, not a GNIS feature (Moyamensing, Southwark)

caveats: Only geocoded offices are kept (about two thirds); short-lived frontier offices are under-represented (Blevins 2021).
Gibson 1840 lists only the top 100 places (>= 4,226).
Moyamensing and Southwark (PA) are landmark points (Moyamensing Prison, Gloria Dei Church), unverified.

sources.post_offices: Blevins and Helbock 2021, US Post Offices, Harvard Dataverse V1, doi:10.7910/DVN/NUKCNA, CC0 1.0; file 4491713 read remotely 2026-11-24
sources.urban_places: Gibson 1998, Census Population Division Working Paper 27, tables 2-7, public domain (research/urban_places_gibson.csv)
sources.urban_coords_override: USGS GNIS geonames map service, Populated Places layer, accessed 2026-11-24; Wikipedia for two landmarks (research/urban_coords_override.csv, R9 section 5)
